speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; can you tell me your baby's gestational age and how old they are in hours? REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: pH: 7.30, PaCO2: 50 mm Hg, PaO2: 60 mm Hg, HCO3-: 24 mEq/L, Base_Excess: -5

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood gas shows mild respiratory acidosis and hypoxemia. To differentiate between transient tachypnea of the newborn, respiratory distress syndrome, or sepsis, have you noticed any cyanosis or grunting? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of ground-glass appearance and air bronchograms, combined with respiratory acidosis, strongly suggest Respiratory Distress Syndrome. However, I need to confirm if your baby had a mother with pre-existing diabetes and if surfactant replacement therapy has been administered yet.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms the ground-glass pattern typical of Respiratory Distress Syndrome, and the history of a preterm birth at 32 weeks and maternal gestational diabetes aligns with this diagnosis. Given the confirmed findings and lack of mention of prior surfactant therapy, do you want me to finalize the diagnosis as Respiratory Distress Syndrome? DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
